chapter: Herbie Harper and Rasch's notes on Johnson
title: Langston Hughes and Johnson's lack of ego
summary: Johnson dropped a collaboration with Langston Hughes; Rasch notes he rarely boasted.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: He also indicated that Lenox Avenue was the last street to get rid of the trolley. He mentioned Langston Hughes and he and Langston writing something together. J. C. was disappointed about something in Langston and dropped the relationship. He did tell me that Langston initiated it. He still has the papers, the poem and the music in Wortsborough.

During this conversation he made one of his typical J. C. remarks, quote, "Don't let the same bee sting you twice." I found a real absence of ego in J. C. Johnson, and I think it's important to record this. The only time he ever, quote, "blew his own horn," so to speak, was when he mentioned the story of himself and Langston Hughes. And he said, quote, "I was running kind of hot myself when Langston autographed a book and sent it to me. Then he sent me his second book and asked to get together on something." End quote.
